chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ala' ibn Rizin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (And breathed into him of My Spirit). He (AS) replied, 'A spirit that Allah chose, selected, and created for Himself, and favored over all other spirits, so He commanded and breathed from it into Adam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'Spirit' breathed into Adam according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the 'Spirit' (Ruh) breathed into Adam is not merely a generic soul, but a specific, exalted entity created by Allah for Himself, distinguished by its unique selection and superiority over all other spirits. This interpretation underscores the metaphysical elevation of Adam, linking his creation directly to a divine essence chosen for its inherent excellence, a concept central to Shia theological discussions on the nature of the soul and prophetic lineage.
